# Prune

> Free, MIT-licensed, local-first structural linter for AI-written TypeScript and JavaScript. Finds dead exports, unreachable files, duplicate types, god files, import cycles and near-duplicate functions, and turns them into tasks a coding agent can work and verify. Runs as a CLI, a pre-commit check, and an MCP server.

## When to use Prune

Reach for Prune when you are a coding agent working in a TypeScript or JavaScript repository and:

- you just made or reviewed a large change and want to find what it left behind (unused exports, orphan files, duplicate types): run `prune tasks`
- you are about to delete or rename an export and need to know who uses it: call `safe_to_delete`, `who_uses` or `rename_impact`
- the user asks to clean up, simplify, de-duplicate or shrink the codebase: run `prune tasks` and work the list, verifying each with `prune verify <id>`
- you need a gate so structural debt doesn't grow: `prune check` in pre-commit, `prune scan --baseline --ci` in CI

Prune is not a formatter, type checker or bug finder, and it does not analyze Python, Go or other languages.

## Setup (for agents)

Follow https://prunecode.ai/setup (Markdown: https://prunecode.ai/setup.md). It installs Prune with the repo's package manager, records a baseline, wires `prune check` into the existing hook system, connects MCP, and adds notes to AGENTS.md. Before Prune is installed, use `npx --no-install prune` rather than `npx prune`: an unrelated npm package is named `prune`.

## Commands

- `prune init`: write .prunerc, ignore .prune/
- `prune scan`: findings and score (`--json`, `--baseline`, `--changed REF`, `--ci`)
- `prune check [FILES...]`: pre-commit gate over staged files; fails only on new findings at or above `--fail-on` (default high)
- `prune tasks`: prioritized task checklist (`--json`, `-n`, `--changed`); each task ends with `prune verify <id>`
- `prune baseline`: record current findings so only new ones fail
- `prune fix --apply --check "<typecheck>"`: safe autofix (unexport, delete unreachable files), reverted if the check fails
- `prune verify <id>`: exit 0 once a finding is resolved
- `prune mcp`: MCP over stdio. Tools: tasks, scan, plan, compose_plan, verify, who_uses, safe_to_delete, rename_impact, recent_files

## MCP

- Claude Code: `claude mcp add prune -- npx prune mcp` (or `prune mcp` for the binary install)
- .mcp.json / .cursor/mcp.json: `{ "mcpServers": { "prune": { "command": "npx", "args": ["prune", "mcp"] } } }`
